answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then slash it when a cryptographic audit links that identity to duplicate claims or coordinated votes. A public delta in stake-weighted reputation makes fresh accounts carry little influence until they build a costly history; a cipher can protect private audit evidence, while a lantern-style random challenge selects claims to verify. Sybil farms must lock capital across many accounts and risk losing it, so identities are costly rather than free.
